title: Automatic fallback & circuit breaker for smart routing (429/timeout/error thresholds)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an automatic fallback mechanism and per-route circuit breaker logic inside the smart routing layer so that requests are rerouted away from degraded regions/tier/model-variant automatically when service-level signals indicate overload or elevated errors. This ticket covers: (1) defining triggers (429 bursts, timeout windows, and sustained error-rate thresholds), (2) concrete circuit-breaker state machine and backoff policy, (3) integration with routing policies (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants), (4) metrics and alerts, and (5) rollout and chaos tests.
design_decision: We will implement per-[customer,route,model-variant,region] buckets for trigger evaluation to avoid noisy global failures. Circuit breaker states will follow CLOSED -> OPEN -> HALF_OPEN -> CLOSED. Triggers: 429 rate (>= 5% sustained over 1 minute with 5 requests/min baseline), timeout p99 > 5s for 1m, or error rate >= 4% over 5m. Open duration uses exponential backoff starting at 30s up to 20m. On OPEN, routing will: (a) try same model variant in alternative region if available and policy allows, (b) fall back to a lower-cost compatible variant (quantized/safer model) if region unavailable, (c) finally degrade to degrade-mode response (graceful error with retry hints). Decision rationale: per-bucket isolation reduces blast radius; mixing short and long windows captures both bursts and sustained degradations; exponential reopen reduces cascade when service recovers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A simulated region that returns 429s causes smart-router to mark bucket OPEN and route new requests to alternate region/model-variant within 30s. 2) Circuit breaker's OPEN->HALF_OPEN transition retries 5 synthetic probes; if <50% succeed, remain OPEN and escalate. 3) All breaker events emit metric tags: breaker_bucket, trigger_type, region, model_variant, route_id. 4) Grafana dashboard shows breaker states and time-sliced events. 5) No regressions in unit/regression tests and no SLO drops in canary tenants.
implementation_notes: - Leverage existing routing policy engine; add BreakerManager component that subscribes to per-route metrics stream. - Use Redis or in-process consistent store for bucket state with TTL to support multi-instance sync; initial POC will use Redis for correctness. - Add counters and jittered timers to avoid thundering herd on HALF_OPEN. - Expose an admin API to force-open/force-close buckets for incident response. - Ensure fallback respects tenant routing policies (e.g., some tenants opt out of cross-region fallback or lower-tier fallbacks).
tests: Unit tests for breaker state transitions, integration tests using the routing simulator that can inject 429/timeouts/errors per-region, chaos tests in staging that flip region responses, and load tests verifying no increased p99 latency for non-affected buckets. Add canary test group to exercise fallback to quantized model variants and measure quality regression with existing eval prompt set.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime.smartRouting.breakers (default off). 2) Deploy BreakerManager and metrics instrumentation to staging. 3) Run simulation suite and chaos tests for 72 hours. 4) Enable for 5 internal tenants in canary for 48 hours. 5) Gradually ramp to 25% tenant traffic, validate dashboards and alerting, then full rollout. 6) Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and retro. Rollback: disable feature flag + force-close open breakers.
